title: When Does Future Mobility Information Have Packet-Level Value in Vehicular Optical Scheduling?
research_question: When, why, and under which operating regimes does causal trajectory/link prediction change packet-level scheduling relative to reactive scheduling, and when does that information fail to provide robust packet-level value?

claim_boundary.mobility_evidence: controlled synthetic for the corrected service-guard holdout; legacy compact WOMD/proxy outputs are diagnostic only
claim_boundary.optical_link: PC-FMCW/DPSK-informed analytical/simulation model with separately verified Part-A receiver BER evidence

correction.reason: Historical packet deadlines used arrival + N as an inclusive last-service slot, which allowed N+1 service slots. The corrected simulator uses arrival + N - 1 and rejects physical deadlines that are not exactly representable at the configured slot duration.

confirmatory_method.independent_unit: paired holdout seed within operating regime
confirmatory_method.pairing: same deterministic synthetic mobility scenario and traffic trace for candidate and Reactive
confirmatory_method.multiplicity: Holm across four predeclared primary regime comparisons

corrected_primary_result.interpretation: The corrected holdout does not establish a robust incremental goodput advantage or harm for the prospectively selected service_guarded_100 policy relative to Reactive Greedy under the frozen practical-margin/95% CI rule.

evidence_policy.historical_primary: run 34055071988 retained as pre-correction provenance only

required_interpretation.oracle_label: evaluator-only information reference, not a globally optimal offline scheduler
required_interpretation.deadline_semantics: A physical packet deadline must equal an integer number of simulator slots; N slots permit service in exactly N slots including the arrival slot.
